analysis.purpose: The C# structural parser: turns the token stream into a declaration tree (namespace, class, interface, struct, record, enum, delegate, method, property, constructor, indexer, operator) plus a flat list of call sites, deliberately stopping short of a full expression parser because the symbol graph only needs declaration spans, nesting, and call-site heads.
responsibilities: Descend the token stream tolerantly, emitting a declaration per construct
Record nesting so members carry qualified names and member-of edges
Collect call sites in a separate whole-stream pass
Degrade on malformed input by skipping the construct rather than throwing
Track the file namespace so nested types resolve to fully qualified names

businessRules.rule: Not a full expression parser — a tolerant brace/indent-level descent is enough, and is far less surface area to get wrong.
businessRules.rationale: The symbol graph needs spans, nesting and call heads; parsing expressions would add risk without adding graph value.

businessRules.rule: A property is emitted as one symbol; its get/set/init accessor bodies are not descended into separate symbols.
businessRules.rationale: Accessors are implementation detail of one member.

businessRules.rule: Local functions inside method bodies are not extracted, because method bodies are consumed rather than descended.
businessRules.rationale: A documented limitation matching the Java parser.
